rows: Your argument is that the mat belongs to you. Very well. My argument is that you will have to get me there first.
I concede that you can hit hard. I do not concede that hitting hard constitutes a winning argument.
Every time your feet leave the mat, you give up control of the proceedings. I intend to take it.
You can keep the audience waiting if you wish. You cannot postpone the question indefinitely.
A ticket entitles these people to a contest, not an excuse. I expect both of us to honour that.
The running order is an administrative detail. The main event begins when I take the microphone.
That is a declaration, not a verdict. We have yet to hear the evidence.
You are entitled to try to stay upright. I would not make that the cornerstone of your case.
On the matter of effort we agree. On your ability to sustain it, I reserve judgement.
You have identified your own advantage: {strength}. That saves me the trouble of establishing what I need to take away.
Very good. We have established your preferred method: {strength}. Now we can test whether it is sufficient.
I have no personal complaint against you. My objection is to the suggestion that you are going to win.
Raising my voice would not strengthen my argument. I will leave that temptation to you.
Then we agree on the terms. We disagree about the result.
You have made your position clear. What you have not done is answer the objection.
Let us return to the point at issue. I am not interested in a second argument until you have answered the first.
I will grant you that point. You may find the rest of my argument considerably less accommodating.
Accepted. We can dispense with the rest of the speeches.
If your case rests on what you do on the canvas, the first question is how you intend to put me there.
Your striking is not in dispute. Its sufficiency is.
While you are in the air, you have surrendered the means of changing your argument.
The audience has paid for a conclusion. I will not let you adjourn the proceedings.
They are entitled to a full contest. I propose we hold each other to that standard.
I have one point to make to the people who bought tickets: judge the wrestling.
Whatever order the programme lists, my appearance is the one that requires a headline.
Examine the evidence in front of you. That is the standard.
Then you must establish that you can prevent a takedown. Merely stating it is not evidence.
An excellent distinction. Now establish that you can withstand the first strike.
Your opportunity lasts precisely as long as I permit it.
You call it delay. I call it control of the proceedings.
That is a reasonable obligation. I doubt your ability to discharge it.
Your declaration does not constitute the verdict.
You have identified {strength}. I will not dispute the existence of the problem; I will dispute its outcome.
Let the record show that your advantage is {strength}. It is the point on which I intend to cross-examine you.
I have no complaint against you personally. My complaint is with your proposed result.
No raised voices. We can settle the matter on the canvas.
I will not dignify the grievance with a shouting match.
One fall, as the rules state. No accomplices. Those are the terms I am putting before you.
If the canvas is your evidence, let us examine it there.
Try making your case with both feet on the ground.
Remain inside those ropes and answer the question in wrestling terms.
On that much we agree. The result remains contested.
We have not disposed of the first question. Answer it.
I accept that particular point; nothing further.
I anticipate a difficult case. I intend to win it.
My conclusion is simple: I will win.
One clean fall in the centre. No qualifications.
That is all the evidence I intend to present before the bell.
I have prepared my argument. You will see the rest in the ring.
Objection sustained. I have no particulars to offer that establish the charge, and I will not invent them.
A demand for evidence is reasonable. I withdraw the allegation rather than pretend it is a finding.
Very well. The unsupported allegation is not part of the case. The contest remains.
Let the distinction stand. An unproven charge is not a verdict; neither is a speech a wrestling result.
The issue is whether either of us can substantiate our wrestling claims under opposition. The match is the appropriate forum.
We can establish who earns the fall and by what means. Anything beyond that requires evidence we do not yet have.
